issue_context.title: Vim: ctrl-d and ctrl-u bugs when used with `scroll_beyond_last_line` off
issue_context.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [X] Completed

### Describe the bug / provide steps to reproduce it

There are three related buggy behaviors. I'd be happy to split these into separate issues if you'd prefer that.

All of these are with the setting `"scroll_beyond_last_line": "off"`, which matches the behavior of neovim.

1. `ctrl-d` can't reach the bottom of the buffer.
2. If the cursor is already further down than the point it could otherwise reach via `ctrl-d`, it will actually go up.
3. When the cursor is on the last line, `ctrl-u` will scroll up, but the cursor won't move with it. It stays on the last line.

### Environment

Zed: v0.145.1 (Zed)
OS: macOS 14.4.1
Memory: 16 GiB
Architecture: x86_64

### If applicable, add mockups / screenshots to help explain present your vision of the feature

Video showing the first two bugs:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6d0fddd1-3c10-4e53-ba58-13c995708deb

Video showing the third bug:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0ba772d-6798-4bcb-8594-27cf5548f32f

The same commands in neovim:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52ec847d-dac8-4c8c-93d7-b3c6eed907bb


### If applicable, attach your Zed.log file to this issue.

_No response_
comments: I think I have fixes for these issues. I'll open a PR.

review_comments: This is the change that fixes `ctrl-u` when you're on the last line of the file. I'm not sure if this will have any other unintended effects.

I'm storing the starting column due to (I think) a bug in `map.clip_point`, which will move the cursor to the right when passed a display point that is past the last line, even if you provide `Bias::Left`.

There's almost surely a better way to fix this root issue, but using the starting_column after `clip_point` ensures that we attempt to go return to the column we started on, which more closely matches neovim behavior. Neovim's behavior is actually more complex than that, but I think that would be a can of worms for this PR.

This fix isn't necessary for the issue I originally opened. However, when I was writing the test for the original issue, I was running into a difference in behavior between the column that the cursor ended up on between neovim and zed. I can revert this change, but I would likely need to add a hack into the new test to re-adjust the column.
